newsitem.title: USA: Gilead Sciences says will test oral PMPA.
newsitem.headline: Gilead Sciences says will test oral PMPA.

text.p: Gilead Sciences Inc said Wednesday it is enrolling patients in a Phase I/II study to evaluate oral PMPA for the potential treatment of human immunodeficiency virus infection.
The company said this Phase I/II study is being conducted to assess the safety, pharmacokinetics and anti-HIV activity of oral PMPA.
The company said the Phase I/II study is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalating trial that will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and antiviral activity of oral PMPA.
The company said the study is s designed to enroll HIV-infected patients with CD4 counts greater than or equal to 200 cells/mm, and HIV RNA greater than or equal to 10,000 copies/ml.
The company said the patients will be randomly assigned to placebo or active PMPA tablet at one of several different dose levels.
The company said that at each dose level, 10 patients will receive a single dose of oral PMPA or placebo, followed by a six-day observation period.
After determination of safety and tolerability, these patients will be eligible to receive oral PMPA or placebo treatment once daily for an additional four weeks.
The company said escalation to the next higher dose level may take place after data from the lower dose levels are evaluated.
The company said the study will be conducted at three clinical research centers in the United States.
